answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to anchor its identity to one scarce, non-transferable credential earned through hardware attestation and a refundable deposit. Viewed through the prism of cost, creating a fake identity then demands a new verified device, a fresh deposit, and time, so an attacker's expense grows with each sockpuppet while an honest agent pays only once. Like saffron, real credentials are expensive to produce and cheap to verify, and duplicate credentials trigger slashing of the deposit, making mass forgery unprofitable.
